## Left open by the earlier read (RD-019)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule B02 (Blocker). Problem: The stem names two women, so 'she' can still mean Liza after the rewrite. The solution says the reference is now clear, but a clear repair repeats the name or restructures the sentence, for example 'When Ana spoke to Liza, Ana was worried'.
   > Write **"Ana was worried when she spoke to Liza."**
2. Rule L09 (Minor). Problem: The terms payak, tambalan, hugnayan, and sugnay na makapag-iisa/di-makapag-iisa are hard grammar terms with no short English gloss (simple, compound, complex, independent, dependent) on first use.
   > Ang payak na pangungusap ay may isang sugnay na makapag-iisa.
3. Rule L18 (Major). Problem: The original lesson worked a neither...nor compound-subject agreement case (brief L03 quote). The rewrite removed it and teaches only each-of and an interrupting phrase, so a case another tagged exam needs is gone.
   > **Subject-verb agreement** means matching the subject and main verb.
4. Rule L22a (Minor). Problem: This paragraph lists four sentence types in four sentences, over the limit of three.
   > A simple sentence has one independent clause.
5. Rule L22a (Minor). Problem: This paragraph has four sentences, over the limit of three.
   > Maaaring magpahayag ang pandiwa ng kilos, pangyayari, o karanasan.

### Accuracy concerns

1. The pronoun 'she' can still refer to Liza, so the stated fix may not remove the ambiguity that the example claims to repair.
   > Write **"Ana was worried when she spoke to Liza."**
2. The original has no stated link between the two clauses, so the repair adds a cause the stem does not give.
   > One repair for both is **"The office closed early because the storm became stronger."**
